name: Chicken Biryani
description: A layered, aromatic chicken and basmati rice dish with mint, fried onion and whole spices.

ingredient_details.name: Chicken
ingredient_details.note: Bone-in pieces give a richer flavour.

ingredient_details.name: Water
ingredient_details.quantity: as needed for rice and gravy

instructions: Wash the basmati rice until the water runs mostly clear. Soak for 20 minutes, then drain.
Mix the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, chilli powder, turmeric, lemon juice and salt. Rest for at least 20 minutes.
Heat oil and ghee in a heavy pot. Fry the sliced onions until deep golden; reserve a small handful for garnish.
Add bay leaves, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon. Add green chillies and tomatoes; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the marinated chicken and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the outside changes colour and the masala thickens.
Stir in half the mint and coriander. Add the drained rice and gently mix once so the grains do not break.
Add hot water to suit your rice and pot; the liquid should be just enough for the rice to cook. Taste and adjust salt.
Cover tightly. Cook on medium-low for 8 minutes, then on the lowest heat for 12–15 minutes, until the rice is tender and chicken is fully cooked.
Rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff gently and garnish with the reserved fried onion, mint and coriander.
tips: For dum cooking, keep the flame very low and use a thick-bottomed pot or a heat diffuser.
Chicken should reach 74°C / 165°F at the thickest part before serving.

name: Tomato Rice
description: Tomato Rice, a home-style Tamil Nadu dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Cook rice until the grains are separate. Spread it on a plate and let it cool.
Heat oil; splutter mustard seeds and add curry leaves.
Add onion, green chilli, ginger and garlic. Sauté until the onion softens.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Cook until pulpy and the oil begins to show at the edges.
Add the cooled rice and fold gently until every grain is coated.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with curd or papad.

name: Everyday Chicken Curry
description: Everyday Chicken Curry, a home-style Home-style dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Grind the coconut with a little water to a smooth paste and keep aside.
Heat oil in a kadai. Add fennel seeds and curry leaves.
Add onions and sauté until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until its raw smell fades.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Cook until soft and thick.
Add chicken and turn well in the masala for 5 minutes.
Add water, cover and simmer until the chicken is fully cooked, about 20–25 minutes depending on the pieces.
Stir in coconut paste and simmer uncovered for 5–7 minutes until the gravy reaches the thickness you like.

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
description: Vegetable Fried Rice, a home-style Indo-Chinese dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Use cold, separate-grain rice for the best texture.
Heat oil in a wok on high heat. Add garlic and onion; toss for 30 seconds.
Add carrot, beans and capsicum. Stir-fry for 2–3 minutes so the vegetables stay slightly crisp.
Add rice, soy sauce, pepper and a little salt. Toss until hot throughout.
Finish with spring onion and serve immediately.

name: Egg Masala
description: Egg Masala, a home-style South Indian dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Boil eggs for 9–10 minutes, cool, peel and make shallow slits.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Cook until soft and the masala thickens.
Add ½ cup water and simmer to make a gravy.
Add eggs and garam masala. Simmer for 4–5 minutes, turning the eggs gently to coat.
Serve hot with rice, dosa or chapati.

name: Masala Dosa
description: Masala Dosa, a home-style Karnataka / Tamil Nadu dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, peel and roughly mash.
Heat oil. Add mustard seeds, urad dal and curry leaves.
Add onion and green chilli; sauté until soft. Add turmeric, potatoes, salt and ¼ cup water. Mix to make the filling.
Spread a ladle of dosa batter thinly on a hot greased tawa.
Drizzle a little oil. Cook until the underside turns golden.
Place potato masala in the centre, fold and serve with chutney and sambar.

name: Garlic Chicken
description: Garlic Chicken, a home-style Indo-Chinese dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Coat chicken with 1 tbsp corn flour, pepper and a pinch of salt.
Heat oil and cook chicken in batches until browned and cooked through. Set aside.
In the same pan sauté garlic until fragrant, then add onion and capsicum.
Add soy sauce and water; bring to a gentle simmer.
Mix 1 tsp corn flour with 2 tbsp cold water and stir it into the pan.
Return chicken and toss until coated in the glossy sauce. Serve hot.

name: Vegetable Upma
description: Vegetable Upma, a home-style Tamil Nadu dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Dry-roast rava on low heat for 4–5 minutes until aromatic; do not brown. Set aside.
Heat oil or ghee. Add mustard seeds, urad dal and curry leaves.
Add onion, green chilli and carrot. Sauté for 2–3 minutes.
Add water and salt; bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and slowly rain in the rava while stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook on low for 3–4 minutes. Fluff and serve.

name: Tamil Nadu Village Chicken Curry
description: Tamil Nadu Village Chicken Curry, a home-style Tamil Nadu village style dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Grind coconut with ½ cup water to a smooth paste. Crush half the shallots roughly.
Heat oil in a heavy kadai. Add fennel seeds and curry leaves.
Add remaining shallots and sliced onion. Fry until golden at the edges.
Add ginger-garlic paste and crushed shallots; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Cook until the tomatoes turn mushy.
Add chicken and crushed pepper. Toss for 5–6 minutes so the masala coats every piece.
Pour in 1½ cups water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring now and then, until chicken is cooked.
Add coconut paste and simmer uncovered for 6–8 minutes. Adjust water and salt; finish with curry leaves.
tips: For a deeper village-style flavour, use a heavy iron kadai and freshly ground pepper.
Cook chicken thoroughly; the thickest piece should reach 74°C / 165°F.

name: Chettinad Chicken Curry
description: Chettinad Chicken Curry, a home-style Chettinad, Tamil Nadu dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Dry-roast coriander, fennel, cumin, pepper, dry red chillies, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom until aromatic. Cool.
Roast coconut separately until lightly golden. Grind the roasted spices and coconut with a little water into a paste.
Heat oil. Add curry leaves and onions; sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute. Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add chicken and salt. Fry for 5–7 minutes until the chicken is coated in masala.
Add the ground Chettinad paste and 1½ cups water. Mix well.
Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until chicken is completely cooked and gravy thickens.
Finish with fresh curry leaves and serve with rice, dosa or parotta.

name: Kongu Chicken Kulambu
description: Kongu Chicken Kulambu, a home-style Kongu region, Tamil Nadu dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Grind coconut with fennel, cumin and pepper into a smooth masala paste.
Heat oil in a kadai. Add curry leaves and small onions; sauté until lightly golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and tomato. Cook until tomato softens.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, salt and chicken. Roast together for 5 minutes.
Add water, cover and cook until chicken is tender, around 20–30 minutes.
Stir in the coconut-spice paste and simmer for 7–8 minutes until the kulambu thickens.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve with hot rice, idli or dosa.

name: Chicken Pepper Gravy
description: Chicken Pepper Gravy, a home-style Tamil Nadu pepper style dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Coarsely crush the peppercorns. Keep a teaspoon aside for the final seasoning.
Heat oil in a kadai. Add fennel, cumin and curry leaves.
Add sliced onion and shallots. Sauté until golden and lightly caramelised.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw aroma fades.
Add tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, half the crushed pepper and salt. Cook until the tomato becomes pulpy.
Add chicken and roast for 6–8 minutes, turning to coat well in the masala.
Pour in hot water, cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, or until the chicken is fully cooked.
Remove the lid and reduce the gravy to your preferred consistency. Add the reserved pepper and simmer for 2 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving with rice, dosa, idli or parotta.
tips: For a stronger pepper kick, add the reserved crushed pepper at the end rather than cooking all of it for a long time.
Adjust pepper gradually; freshly crushed pepper can be much hotter than pre-ground pepper.

name: Country Chicken Kulambu
description: Country Chicken Kulambu, a home-style Tamil Nadu country-style dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Dry-roast coriander, fennel and pepper. Grind with coconut and a little water.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker or heavy pot. Add curry leaves and small onions; sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes. Cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, salt and country chicken. Roast for 5 minutes.
Add water. Pressure-cook for the time needed for your chicken to become tender; native chicken may take longer than broiler chicken.
Open only after pressure has released. Add the ground coconut masala.
Simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes until the gravy thickens. Check that the chicken is tender and fully cooked.
tips: Country chicken usually needs more cooking time than broiler chicken. Use tenderness, not the clock alone, to judge doneness.

name: Chicken Sukka
description: Chicken Sukka, a home-style Tamil Nadu dry masala dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Coarsely grind fennel, pepper and coconut.
Heat oil; add curry leaves and onions. Sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook briefly.
Add chicken, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Mix well.
Cover and cook on low, stirring occasionally. Add a splash of water only if needed.
When chicken is cooked and tender, uncover and roast until most moisture evaporates.
Add the coconut-pepper mixture and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until the masala coats the chicken.

name: Pepper Chicken Fry
description: Pepper Chicken Fry, a home-style South Indian pepper fry dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Heat oil and add fennel and curry leaves.
Add onions and sauté until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add chicken, salt and half the crushed pepper. Mix and cook covered until chicken is done, adding a splash of water if needed.
Remove the lid and roast until the moisture dries and the pieces are lightly browned.
Add remaining pepper and lemon juice. Toss and serve hot.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
description: Paneer Butter Masala, a home-style Punjabi-inspired dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Simmer tomatoes, onion, ginger, garlic and cashews with ½ cup water until soft. Cool and blend smooth.
Heat oil and butter in a pan. Add the blended sauce and cook for 5–7 minutes.
Add chilli powder, garam masala, salt and water to adjust thickness.
Add paneer and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes.
Stir in cream, warm through without boiling hard, and serve with naan or rice.

name: Mutton Biryani
description: Mutton Biryani, a home-style Tamil Nadu style dish with a balanced, aromatic masala.
instructions: Wash and soak rice for 20 minutes. Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, chilli powder, turmeric and salt.
Heat oil and ghee in a pressure cooker. Fry onions until golden; reserve a little for garnish.
Add green chillies, tomatoes, mint and coriander. Cook until tomatoes soften.
Add marinated mutton and sauté for 8–10 minutes.
Add water and pressure-cook until mutton is tender. Cooking time depends on the cut and age of the meat.
Measure the remaining gravy and add water so there is enough liquid for the rice. Bring to a boil.
Add drained rice. Mix gently, cover and cook on low until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 10 minutes. Fluff gently and garnish with fried onion and herbs.

name: Afghani Chicken
description: Juicy chicken marinated in a mild, creamy white mixture of yogurt, cashew, cream, aromatics and warm spices, then grilled or pan-seared until lightly charred.

ingredient_details.name: Chicken
ingredient_details.quantity: 750 g, medium pieces or boneless cubes
ingredient_details.note: Make 2–3 shallow slits in bone-in pieces so the marinade reaches inside.

ingredient_details.name: Cashews
ingredient_details.note: Soak in hot water for 15 minutes, then grind to a smooth paste.

ingredient_details.name: Extra cream and coriander
ingredient_details.quantity: 1 tbsp cream and 2 tbsp chopped coriander

instructions: Pat the chicken dry. If using bone-in pieces, make 2–3 shallow cuts in each piece; this helps the marinade season the meat evenly.
Grind the soaked cashews with 1–2 tablespoons of water until completely smooth. A coarse paste can make the coating grainy.
In a bowl, whisk together yogurt, cream, cashew paste, ginger-garlic paste, ground green chilli, lemon juice, pepper, cumin, cardamom, garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, oil and salt.

Add the chicken and turn each piece until thoroughly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours; 4–6 hours gives a deeper flavour. Do not leave raw chicken at room temperature while marinating.
Take the chicken out of the refrigerator 15 minutes before cooking. Preheat an oven or air fryer to 200°C, or heat a heavy grill pan or skillet over medium heat.

For oven or air fryer cooking, arrange the pieces in a single layer and cook for about 18–25 minutes, turning once halfway. For a skillet, cook in batches with a little oil, turning regularly so the creamy coating browns without burning.
Check the thickest part of the largest piece with a food thermometer. Chicken is ready when it reaches 74°C / 165°F; bone-in pieces may need extra time depending on size.
Brush with melted butter during the last 2 minutes. For light char, place under a hot grill briefly or sear each side in a hot pan, watching closely because the dairy marinade can darken quickly.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes. Finish with a little cream and chopped coriander, then serve hot with naan, roomali roti, pulao or salad.
tips: For the characteristic pale Afghani-style finish, keep chilli powder and turmeric out of the marinade; use green chilli and pepper for gentle heat.
If the marinade is too runny, add 1 tablespoon of extra cashew paste. A thick coating clings to the chicken and browns more evenly.
Cooking time depends on piece size and appliance. Use 74°C / 165°F at the thickest part as the doneness check.
substitutions: Replace cashews with blanched almonds if needed; the flavour will be slightly different.
For a lighter marinade, replace half the cream with thick yogurt.
For a stovetop version, use a heavy skillet on medium-low heat and cover briefly after searing so thick pieces cook through.
